Articles for Deletion — what the discussions look like¶

Descriptives for the AfD corpus: every deletion discussion on English Wikipedia through the 2025-01-25 dump (and how the 37k study sample sits inside it).

This notebook is analysis only. Loading data + any repairs (e.g., backfill API collections of missing data or pages that turned out to be redirects to a full discussion) live in afd_load.py. The working notebooks to figure out issues in collected data are: afd_case_descriptives.ipynb and afd_case_descriptives_1.ipynb

Groups¶

We split the deletion cases into a few subsets:

group meaning
gone the article does not exist today
sample the 37k study set — surviving, 2007–2022, article ≥30 days old at nomination, cleared the rough match
surviving_nonsample survived, not in the sample
surviving the union of the last two — a reference line in the figures, not a fourth group

Note¶

A discussion is measured over its first 30 days. 98%+ of human edits land inside that window; what follows is almost entirely archival bot activity. Measures named *_days or n_* are window-bounded unless stated.

"Surviving" means the page exists, not that the article ended in a keep decision. Roughly a third of surviving cases have a revision history that begins after their own nomination — deleted, then recreated — and a share of the rest are now redirects. we treat the label as a page-state fact, not an outcome.

Participation counts anyone who edited the page. That includes the nominator, the closer, relisting bots' human counterparts and deletion-sorting regulars. n_editors counts them; n_discussants counts only editors whose participation was not only nominating and/or closing. The two differ by about 1.6 on average. We just need to think of the numbers in relative terms.

Decisions are parsed from the text. We were able to parse ~99.7%; the failures are concentrated pre-2007, when closes were often unbolded. This is fine, we have some imperfect figs below as a result but our analysis will start 2007 onwards. Cases with no parseable result are NaN, not misc (which is a parent category of some other types of decisions).

def summary(cols, frame=None, groups=three):
    """median (IQR) per group, plus the sample/nonsample ratio -- the table to quote."""
    F = D if frame is None else frame
    out = {}
    for g in groups:
        x = F.pipe(panel, g)[cols]
        out[g] = (x.median().round(2).astype(str) + "  ("
                  + x.quantile(.25).round(2).astype(str) + "–"
                  + x.quantile(.75).round(2).astype(str) + ")")
    t = pd.DataFrame(out)
    t["sample / nonsample"] = (F.pipe(panel, "sample")[cols].median()
                               / F.pipe(panel, "surviving_nonsample")[cols].median()).round(2)
    return t

SHOW = HEADLINE + ["n_editors", "n_edits", "size_chars"]
summary(sorted(set(SHOW), key=SHOW.index))

# a random 10 discussions per group, to read by hand
from IPython.display import HTML, display

N_CASES, SEED = 10, 0
SHOW_C = ["case_title", "grp", "afd_year", "decision_flat"] + HEADLINE + ["n_editors", "discussion"]
C = D.join(cases.set_index("afd_pageid")[["case_title", "afd_discussion_url"]])
C["discussion"] = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/" + C.afd_discussion_url

def show_cases(frame, col, levels, n=N_CASES, seed=SEED):
    """n random discussions per level of `col`, with a clickable link to each."""
    parts = []
    for k in levels:
        t = frame[frame[col].eq(k)]
        t = t.sample(min(n, len(t)), random_state=seed)[SHOW_C].sort_values("afd_year")
        parts.append(f"<h3>{k} ({len(frame[frame[col].eq(k)]):,} cases)</h3>"
                     + t.round(2).to_html(render_links=True, escape=True))
    display(HTML("\n".join(parts)))

show_cases(C, "grp", three)

3. Who shows up¶

  • one-timer: only contributes once to one discussion ever
  • regular: top 1% of contributors by discussion count
  • occasional: neither regulars nor one-timers (admittedly, a very loose category with wide range)
  • "green": participated in < 10 prior AfDs before this one

Sometimes we consider "discussants" instead of "editors," to get rid of mundane edits like administrative closing edits.

# who are they? samples of each participant class to look up by hand
from IPython.display import HTML, display

N, SEED = 25, 0
SHOW_E = ["n_discussions", "n_afd_edits", "first_afd_edit", "last_afd_edit", "afd_tenure_days"]
name = editors_w.index.str.replace(" ", "_")
ew = editors_w.assign(
    user_page="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:" + name,
    contribs="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Contributions/" + name + "?namespace=4",  # Wikipedia: pages only
)

samples = {
    "regular (top 25)": ew[ew.cls.eq("regular")].nlargest(N, "n_discussions"),
    "regular (random)": ew[ew.cls.eq("regular")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
    "occasional":       ew[ew.cls.eq("occasional")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
    "one_timer":        ew[ew.cls.eq("one_timer")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
}
parts = []
for lab, t in samples.items():
    t = (t[SHOW_E + ["user_page", "contribs"]].sort_values("n_discussions", ascending=False)
          .round({"afd_tenure_days": 0}))
    parts.append(f"<h3>{lab}</h3>" + t.to_html(render_links=True, escape=True))
page = "\n".join(parts)
display(HTML(page))                                  # clickable in the notebook

with open("editor_samples.html", "w") as f:          # same tables, open in a browser
    f.write(f"<!doctype html><meta charset='utf-8'><title>AfD editor samples</title>"
            f"<style>body{{font-family:sans-serif;margin:16px}}table{{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:13px}}"
            f"td,th{{border:1px solid #ccc;padding:3px 6px}}</style>{page}")

4. Outcomes¶

gone is almost entirely delete, so comparing measures across decisions on the whole corpus mostly restates the group split. The informative cut is within the surviving cases, where all five outcomes occur in usable numbers and every article was kept either way.

In [13]:
dec_counts = (pd.concat({g: panel(D, g).decision_flat.value_counts() for g in three}, axis=1)
                .reindex(DEC_ORDER).fillna(0).astype(int))
print(dec_counts.to_string())
print("\nno parseable decision:",
      {g: int(panel(D, g).decision_flat.isna().sum()) for g in three})

share = 100 * dec_counts / dec_counts.sum()
a = share.T.plot.bar(stacked=True, rot=0, figsize=(7.5, 4), ylabel="% of labelled cases",
                     color=[DEC_COLORS[k] for k in DEC_ORDER])
a.legend(title="decision", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc="upper left", frameon=False)
a.figure.tight_layout()

                  gone  sample  surviving_nonsample
decision_flat                                      
keep              1597   26781                32303
no_consensus      1304    6318                 9137
redirect_merge    1739     924                31236
delete          187391    1532                27622
misc              2310    2006                 4260

no parseable decision: {'gone': 96, 'sample': 35, 'surviving_nonsample': 101}

The cases in our sample (~37k) have a distinct composition; a lot more of them are keep cases or were difficult to find consensus for. I think this helps us see them as "edge cases" where deletion was very tetchy.

# a random 10 discussions per decision (all groups -- `grp` shows which side each came from)
show_cases(C, "decision_flat", DEC_ORDER)

5. The study sample¶

The 37k sample was carved out of the surviving cases by three filters: nomination year, article age at nomination, and clearing the topic-vector rough match. The slices below apply the first two on their own, so the difference each one makes is visible separately.

uncensored drops cases nominated after the dump ended, whose 30-day window is only partly observed so it's got incomplete data.

Articles for Deletion — what the discussions look like¶

Descriptives for the AfD corpus: every deletion discussion on English Wikipedia through the 2025-01-25 dump (and how the 37k study sample sits inside it).

This notebook is analysis only. Loading data + any repairs (e.g., backfill API collections of missing data or pages that turned out to be redirects to a full discussion) live in afd_load.py. The working notebooks to figure out issues in collected data are: afd_case_descriptives.ipynb and afd_case_descriptives_1.ipynb

Groups¶

We split the deletion cases into a few subsets:

group meaning
gone the article does not exist today
sample the 37k study set — surviving, 2007–2022, article ≥30 days old at nomination, cleared the rough match
surviving_nonsample survived, not in the sample
surviving the union of the last two — a reference line in the figures, not a fourth group

Note¶

A discussion is measured over its first 30 days. 98%+ of human edits land inside that window; what follows is almost entirely archival bot activity. Measures named *_days or n_* are window-bounded unless stated.

"Surviving" means the page exists, not that the article ended in a keep decision. Roughly a third of surviving cases have a revision history that begins after their own nomination — deleted, then recreated — and a share of the rest are now redirects. we treat the label as a page-state fact, not an outcome.

Participation counts anyone who edited the page. That includes the nominator, the closer, relisting bots' human counterparts and deletion-sorting regulars. n_editors counts them; n_discussants counts only editors whose participation was not only nominating and/or closing. The two differ by about 1.6 on average. We just need to think of the numbers in relative terms.

Decisions are parsed from the text. We were able to parse ~99.7%; the failures are concentrated pre-2007, when closes were often unbolded. This is fine, we have some imperfect figs below as a result but our analysis will start 2007 onwards. Cases with no parseable result are NaN, not misc (which is a parent category of some other types of decisions).

def summary(cols, frame=None, groups=three):
    """median (IQR) per group, plus the sample/nonsample ratio -- the table to quote."""
    F = D if frame is None else frame
    out = {}
    for g in groups:
        x = F.pipe(panel, g)[cols]
        out[g] = (x.median().round(2).astype(str) + "  ("
                  + x.quantile(.25).round(2).astype(str) + "–"
                  + x.quantile(.75).round(2).astype(str) + ")")
    t = pd.DataFrame(out)
    t["sample / nonsample"] = (F.pipe(panel, "sample")[cols].median()
                               / F.pipe(panel, "surviving_nonsample")[cols].median()).round(2)
    return t

SHOW = HEADLINE + ["n_editors", "n_edits", "size_chars"]
summary(sorted(set(SHOW), key=SHOW.index))

# a random 10 discussions per group, to read by hand
from IPython.display import HTML, display

N_CASES, SEED = 10, 0
SHOW_C = ["case_title", "grp", "afd_year", "decision_flat"] + HEADLINE + ["n_editors", "discussion"]
C = D.join(cases.set_index("afd_pageid")[["case_title", "afd_discussion_url"]])
C["discussion"] = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/" + C.afd_discussion_url

def show_cases(frame, col, levels, n=N_CASES, seed=SEED):
    """n random discussions per level of `col`, with a clickable link to each."""
    parts = []
    for k in levels:
        t = frame[frame[col].eq(k)]
        t = t.sample(min(n, len(t)), random_state=seed)[SHOW_C].sort_values("afd_year")
        parts.append(f"<h3>{k} ({len(frame[frame[col].eq(k)]):,} cases)</h3>"
                     + t.round(2).to_html(render_links=True, escape=True))
    display(HTML("\n".join(parts)))

show_cases(C, "grp", three)

3. Who shows up¶

  • one-timer: only contributes once to one discussion ever
  • regular: top 1% of contributors by discussion count
  • occasional: neither regulars nor one-timers (admittedly, a very loose category with wide range)
  • "green": participated in < 10 prior AfDs before this one

Sometimes we consider "discussants" instead of "editors," to get rid of mundane edits like administrative closing edits.

from IPython.display import HTML, display

N, SEED = 25, 0
SHOW_E = ["n_discussions", "n_afd_edits", "first_afd_edit", "last_afd_edit", "afd_tenure_days"]
name = editors_w.index.str.replace(" ", "_")
ew = editors_w.assign(
    user_page="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:" + name,
    contribs="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Contributions/" + name + "?namespace=4",  # Wikipedia: pages only
)

samples = {
    "regular (top 25)": ew[ew.cls.eq("regular")].nlargest(N, "n_discussions"),
    "regular (random)": ew[ew.cls.eq("regular")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
    "occasional":       ew[ew.cls.eq("occasional")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
    "one_timer":        ew[ew.cls.eq("one_timer")].sample(N, random_state=SEED),
}
parts = []
for lab, t in samples.items():
    t = (t[SHOW_E + ["user_page", "contribs"]].sort_values("n_discussions", ascending=False)
          .round({"afd_tenure_days": 0}))
    parts.append(f"<h3>{lab}</h3>" + t.to_html(render_links=True, escape=True))
page = "\n".join(parts)
display(HTML(page))                                  # clickable in the notebook

with open("editor_samples.html", "w") as f:          # same tables, open in a browser
    f.write(f"<!doctype html><meta charset='utf-8'><title>AfD editor samples</title>"
            f"<style>body{{font-family:sans-serif;margin:16px}}table{{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:13px}}"
            f"td,th{{border:1px solid #ccc;padding:3px 6px}}</style>{page}")

4. Outcomes¶

gone is almost entirely delete, so comparing measures across decisions on the whole corpus mostly restates the group split. The informative cut is within the surviving cases, where all five outcomes occur in usable numbers and every article was kept either way.

In [13]:
dec_counts = (pd.concat({g: panel(D, g).decision_flat.value_counts() for g in three}, axis=1)
                .reindex(DEC_ORDER).fillna(0).astype(int))
print(dec_counts.to_string())
print("\nno parseable decision:",
      {g: int(panel(D, g).decision_flat.isna().sum()) for g in three})

share = 100 * dec_counts / dec_counts.sum()
a = share.T.plot.bar(stacked=True, rot=0, figsize=(7.5, 4), ylabel="% of labelled cases",
                     color=[DEC_COLORS[k] for k in DEC_ORDER])
a.legend(title="decision", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc="upper left", frameon=False)
a.figure.tight_layout()

                  gone  sample  surviving_nonsample
decision_flat                                      
keep              1597   26781                32303
no_consensus      1304    6318                 9137
redirect_merge    1739     924                31236
delete          187391    1532                27622
misc              2310    2006                 4260

no parseable decision: {'gone': 96, 'sample': 35, 'surviving_nonsample': 101}

The cases in our sample (~37k) have a distinct composition; a lot more of them are keep cases or were difficult to find consensus for. I think this helps us see them as "edge cases" where deletion was very tetchy.

In [14]:
# a random 10 discussions per decision (all groups -- `grp` shows which side each came from)
show_cases(C, "decision_flat", DEC_ORDER)

Sy = D[D.grp.ne("gone")]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(15, 3.8))
for a, col in zip(ax, HEADLINE):
    data = [Sy.loc[Sy.decision_flat.eq(k), col].dropna() for k in DEC_ORDER]
    bp = a.boxplot(data, showfliers=False, patch_artist=True, medianprops=dict(color="k", lw=1.3))
    for b, k in zip(bp["boxes"], DEC_ORDER):
        b.set_facecolor(DEC_COLORS[k]); b.set_alpha(.6); b.set_edgecolor(DEC_COLORS[k])
    a.set_xticks(range(1, len(DEC_ORDER) + 1), DEC_ORDER, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=7)
    a.set_title(LAB[col], loc="left", fontsize=9)
fig.suptitle("Surviving cases: how the discussion differed by outcome", x=.06, ha="left", fontsize=13)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, .9])

5. The study sample¶

The 37k sample was carved out of the surviving cases by three filters: nomination year, article age at nomination, and clearing the topic-vector rough match. The slices below apply the first two on their own, so the difference each one makes is visible separately.

uncensored drops cases nominated after the dump ended, whose 30-day window is only partly observed so it's got incomplete data.

In [17]:
slices = {
    "surviving (all)":                       S,
    "uncensored, all years":                 S[~S.censored],
    f"time only ({FIRST_YEAR}-{LAST_YEAR})": S[S.afd_year.between(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR)],
    "age only (>= 30d)":                     S[S.age_at_nom_days >= 30],
    "sample":                                S[S.grp.eq("sample")],
}
for k, v in slices.items():
    print(f"{k:34s} n={len(v):>7,}  pre-{FIRST_YEAR} {100*v.afd_year.lt(FIRST_YEAR).mean():5.1f}%  "
          f"censored {100*v.censored.mean():5.2f}%")

print(f"\nrecreated after their own nomination: {100*S.age_at_nom_days.lt(0).mean():.1f}% of surviving cases")
print("(the >= 30d filter removes all of them, since their age is negative)")

slice_med = pd.DataFrame({k: v[HEADLINE + ["n_editors"]].median() for k, v in slices.items()})
slice_med.loc["n_cases"] = [len(v) for v in slices.values()]
slice_med.round(2)
